Guessing without the image

Two shortcuts a model could use without looking: always giving a template's most common answer, or answering with a name the question itself mentions. High shares mean the template leaks its answer and needs rebalancing.

TemplateTasksMost common answerAlways-guess scoreAnswer named in question

Model evaluation

Each sampled task was asked twice: with its image, and without it. Reference answers come from the scene data, never from a model, so a wrong model answer is the model's mistake unless the human audit finds otherwise. Contrast pairs ask the same question about a minimally edited image with a different answer; a model that reads the image gets both right. Sample: 90 of 150 tasks, spread across templates.

Where each model breaks

Accuracy with the image at each difficulty level. A model breaks at the first level where it answers fewer than 80% right. Every level passes the same gates, so a careful person can answer each task.

Phone photos

150 tasks have a photo twin: the same image seen at a slight angle on a desk, with uneven light, a soft glare, a little blur, sensor noise and JPEG compression. The question and the answer are unchanged; a perspective view keeps which tick a needle points at and what connects to what. The gates were run again on each photo, with the label positions mapped through the same perspective.

Tesseract read back 0 of 0 labels from the photos (from the clean images: 0 of 0).

Contrast pairs

150 of 150 tasks have a twin: the same question about an image where one thing was edited so the answer changes (a bar, a needle, a cable's end, a valve), and nothing else moves. The median edit is 1% of the scale (the value axis, a dial, a set of ports). Both images pass the same gates. A model that answers from the question text alone can't get both right.

OCR read-back

An independent check of the grounding gate, which trusts the renderer's layout record. Every label a question depends on was cropped out of the final PNG and read by tesseract 5.5.3, an OCR engine unrelated to the models being evaluated. A label counts as read back when the OCR text matches what was drawn (characters OCR commonly confuses, such as O and 0, count as equal). The crops below show what OCR saw.
